title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: In an agent run, the model asks for the calendar and then, on its next call, answers using the calendar result. In a basic setup, how does the model have the calendar result on that second call?

options.text: The program sends that result again inside the second request
The model stored the result when it first saw it earlier
The model fetches it from the booking system by itself
The provider's servers remember it between the two calls

items.stem: Your assistant's system prompt plus tool definitions total 1,500 tokens and the student's question is 100 tokens. The model makes three calls: it requests a tool (50 tokens), gets a 400-token result, requests another tool (50 tokens), gets a 600-token result, then writes its final answer. Each call sends the whole history so far. How many input tokens are sent in total across the three calls?
A student passes laser cutter training on Monday and returns on Thursday for a new session. Which design lets the assistant know about the training on Thursday at a low token cost?

options.text: Choose a model with a larger window and hope it keeps Monday's chat
Save a short record of the training and load it when the session starts
Paste the complete Monday transcript into the system prompt for every session
Tell the model in its instructions to remember every student it meets

items.stem: When a long conversation nears the window limit, the program can have the model summarize it and start a fresh window from that summary. What is this technique called? Answer in one word.
The makerspace has a 150-page set of manuals. Which approach best controls cost and keeps the model focused on the right information for each question?

options.text: Put all 150 pages into the system prompt so every answer can use them
Rely on the model's training, since it has read many similar manuals
Split the manuals into chunks and load only the few that match
Save the whole manual set as a note and load it every session
